$comment: The contract-binding ledger for design-lab/schemas/contracts/. One row per schema, one row per route src/design_lab/http_service.py dispatches on. Re-checked on every run by design-lab/scripts/verify_contract_bindings.py: a BINDING row's named producer/consumer must still exist and still contain the declared version string, and an INERT row must state what is actually true rather than describing unimplemented work as pending. Paths are repo-relative; instance and test refs are path:line.

status_vocabulary.BINDING: a place in src/ produces or consumes this exact shape and names this version
status_vocabulary.INERT: nothing in src/ produces or consumes this shape; the row says what exists instead

route_kind_vocabulary.BOUND_SCHEMA: the payload is validated by the named schema file against the named emitter
route_kind_vocabulary.SCHEMA_LESS: no schema validates this payload; the reason states why, and a version-bearing row must state the debt outright

Re-bound 2026-10-08. The route no longer answers with the bare receipt document: it answers with the design-lab/delivery-receipt-readback/v1 envelope, whose `receipt` member is that document returned verbatim and whose new members resolve each deliverable's rollback reference against the asset ledger. The document is not extended, because it signs its own bytes with receipt_sha256; the resolution therefore travels beside it, and this row binds the envelope schema and the emitter that writes its version. Both still hold: NativeDelivery.readback() reaches the same _load() that delivery_receipt.loads() re-verifies on every read, and test_delivery_evidence_ui_contract.py pins that the envelope carries the stored document rather than a rebuilt one. The two refusals keep their own codes: 404 DELIVERY_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND means no receipt was recorded for this ACTIVE version, 409 DELIVERY_RECEIPT_UNVERIFIED means a stored document contradicts its own bytes and the service will not certify them.

No schema validates this envelope -- named as debt, not as an unremarkable read. The decisions it wraps ARE bound (each is a design-lab/rights-decision/v1 document, validated by assurance/rights_ledger.py on the way in and re-validated from the stored bytes on the way out); src/design_lab/rights_review.py writes the envelope's own schemaVersion while nothing describes the envelope. The word a reader can be misled by is rights_clearance: CLEARED requires at least one filed use scope AND a current APPROVED for every filed scope, an empty ledger reads NOT_REVIEWED rather than 0-of-0 cleared, and PENDING_REVIEW is only ever a word a human filed -- never one the facade infers. design-lab/tests/test_rights_http.py asserts those rules against real responses. Closing this the way the jury readback was closed needs a rights-readback.schema.json plus a payload case in design-lab/scripts/verify_route_payload_contracts.py; that is not claimed here because it was not done.

The body's exact key set is the contract's own property names, read from the loaded schema (src/design_lab/rights_review.py write_fields) rather than restated in the dispatcher, so an unknown field is refused instead of dropped; the document is then validated against this schema before the row is written (src/design_lab/assurance/rights_ledger.py _validate_against_contract). The enum, the required trio and additionalProperties:false all come from the file named here. The one thing the schema cannot express is checked beside it: an actor that names automation is refused by name, and the signing kind is a column on the row because the closed contract has no field for it.

Closing this the way the jury readback was closed needs a research-readback.schema.json plus a payload case in design-lab/scripts/verify_route_payload_contracts.py; that is not claimed here because it was not done.

The required trio, the confidence enum, additionalProperties:false and the notDesignRule const all come from that file -- no field list is copied into Python, and the source-list field is located by structure (the required field declared as an array), not by a hardcoded name.
